--- title: "Logistic regression with a binary predictor" format: html: df-print: kable toc: true toc-depth: 3 number-sections: true --- # Introduction This notebook extends the treatment example from [logistic-regression foundations](logistic-intro.qmd). We focus on the two arms that make a binary treatment predictor: `waitlist` and `therapist-guided`. Our question is: > Among participants in these two arms, how does the estimated probability of > treatment response differ for therapist-guided treatment versus > waitlist? The target is the **therapist-guided minus waitlist probability difference**. We will use the corresponding odds ratio to read logistic-regression output, but the probability difference is the primary clinical result. # Packages and data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(here) library(broom) library(marginaleffects) options( marginaleffects_print_omit = c("s.value"), marginaleffects_print_style = ifelse(interactive(), "summary", "tinytable") ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df_binary <- read_csv2(here("data", "steps_clean.csv")) |> filter(!is.na(lsas_screen), !is.na(lsas_post)) |> mutate( # The second level is the event modelled by binomial glm(). lsas_response = factor( if_else((lsas_screen - lsas_post) / lsas_screen >= 0.30, "Response", "No response"), levels = c("No response", "Response") ), trt = factor( trt, levels = c("waitlist", "therapist-guided", "self-guided") ) ) |> filter(trt %in% c("waitlist", "therapist-guided")) |> droplevels() df_binary |> count(trt, lsas_response, .drop = FALSE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|trt |lsas_response | n| |:----------------|:-------------|--:| |waitlist |No response | 52| |waitlist |Response | 6| |therapist-guided |No response | 23| |therapist-guided |Response | 31|
::: ::: `Response` means that LSAS decreases by at least 30% from baseline. As in [logistic-regression foundations](logistic-intro.qmd), this is a teaching outcome, not a diagnosis or a remission definition. The factor order makes `High` the first level, so that the binomial model estimates the probability of the second level: treatment response. We explicitly make waitlist the reference group. The treatment contrast shown by the coefficient will therefore be therapist-guided minus waitlist. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} levels(df_binary$trt) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "waitlist" "therapist-guided" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} contrasts(df_binary$trt) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` therapist-guided waitlist 0 therapist-guided 1 ``` ::: ::: # A logistic model for two treatment groups For participant $i$, let $Y_i$ indicate treatment response. The model is $$ \operatorname{logit}\left[P(Y_i = \text{Response} \mid trt_i)\right] = \beta_0 + \beta_1\,\mathbf{1}\{trt_i = \text{therapist-guided}\}. $$ Here, $\beta_0$ is the log-odds of response in the waitlist group, and $\beta_1$ is the therapist-guided-versus-waitlist log-odds difference. These are the quantities that `glm()` estimates directly. They are not yet the most clinically intelligible quantities. | Treatment group | Linear predictor | Model-derived probability | |---|---:|---:| | waitlist | $\beta_0$ | $\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\beta_0)$ | | therapist-guided | $\beta_0 + \beta_1$ | $\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\beta_0 + \beta_1)$ | ## Fit and interpret the model ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mod_binary_trt <- stats::glm( lsas_response ~ trt, family = binomial, data = df_binary ) p_binary_trt <- avg_predictions( mod_binary_trt, by = "trt", type = "response" ) diff_binary_trt <- avg_comparisons( mod_binary_trt, variables = list(trt = c("waitlist", "therapist-guided")), type = "response" ) or_binary_trt <- tidy( mod_binary_trt, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE ) |> filter(term == "trttherapist-guided") ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Model interpretation The estimated probability of treatment response is **10.3%** for waitlist (95% CI **2.5%** to **18.2%**) and **57.4%** for therapist-guided treatment (95% CI **44.2%** to **70.6%**). Compared with waitlist, therapist-guided treatment **increases** the estimated probability by **47.1 percentage points** (therapist-guided minus waitlist = **47.1 percentage points**; 95% CI **31.7** to **62.4 percentage points**). This is an unadjusted contrast within the restricted two-arm sample. The associated therapist-guided-versus-waitlist **odds ratio** is **11.68** (95% CI **4.54** to **34.62**). It is a ratio of the odds of response, not a probability ratio and not a 47.1-percentage-point change. ::: ## Display probabilities and the probability difference ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p_binary_trt ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
trt Estimate Std. Error z Pr(>|z|) 2.5 % 97.5 %
Type: response
waitlist 0.103 0.0400 2.59 0.00968 0.0251 0.182
therapist-guided 0.574 0.0673 8.53 < 0.001 0.4422 0.706
``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} diff_binary_trt ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
Estimate Std. Error z Pr(>|z|) 2.5 % 97.5 %
Type: response
0.471 0.0783 6.01 <0.001 0.317 0.624
``` ::: ::: The estimated probability difference is calculated after transforming the model to the response scale. It answers a different question from the printed log-odds coefficient: how many percentage points higher or lower is the modelled probability in one group than the other? ## Visualise the group probabilities ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_predictions(mod_binary_trt, by = "trt", type = "response") + labs( title = "Estimated probability of treatment response", subtitle = "Waitlist versus therapist-guided treatment; 95% confidence intervals", x = "Treatment group", y = "Probability of treatment response" ) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](logistic-one-binary-predictor_files/figure-html/plot-binary-treatment-probabilities-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: # Log-odds and odds ratios The logistic model is linear on the **log-odds** scale. Exponentiating $\beta_1$ gives the therapist-guided-versus-waitlist odds ratio: $$ \exp(\beta_1) = \frac{\text{odds of response with therapist-guided treatment}} {\text{odds of response with waitlist}}. $$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} or_binary_trt ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|term | estimate| std.error| statistic| p.value| conf.low| conf.high| |:-------------------|--------:|---------:|---------:|-------:|--------:|---------:| |trttherapist-guided | 11.68116| 0.5114807| 4.805611| 1.5e-06| 4.542373| 34.6221|
::: ::: An odds ratio larger than 1 means higher *odds* of response in the therapist-guided group. It cannot be read as a percentage-point increase, because the same odds ratio implies different probability differences at different baseline probabilities. Report the model-derived probabilities and their probability difference when the clinical question concerns chances of an outcome. # Summary In this chapter you learned to: - restrict the STePS data to a binary treatment comparison and set waitlist as the reference category; - fit a binary logistic model with `stats::glm(..., family = binomial)`; - report treatment-specific probabilities and the therapist-guided-minus-waitlist probability difference with 95% CIs; and - interpret the associated odds ratio as a ratio of odds rather than a probability difference.
